title: How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges
summary: NH introduces evolving sets alongside evolving rep ranges and explains his 'elevator' progression: reps and sets climb within a range, then weight goes up and reps reset, so the low point of volume keeps rising. Strength work drives the program, so other lifts' volume curves must be offset to keep tonnage stable.
claims: A rep range that gives no method of progression is a bad rep range; a range is just numbers
Evolving rep ranges can apply to sets as well as reps; more variables add flexibility but complexity
Novices progress fine on fixed schemes like 5x5 or 3x5 and should use evolving ranges only on 8-12 or 6-10 accessory work
Once strength progression slows, bring evolving rep ranges into strength work
Fast novice-style progression isn't realistic or necessary later
Non-novice bodybuilders should get most tonnage from variations and accessories, not strength work
Strength work is the backbone of the program; it provides little tonnage but high-intensity peaks that drive progression, and must never disappear
His elevator scheme: 1-3 sets of 2-5 reps, going 2, then 3-2, then 4-3-2, then 5-4-3, then add 10 lb and restart at 2
After each weight jump volume drops but tonnage stays slightly above the previous cycle's low point, so tonnage constantly progresses
Evolving sets cause dramatic volume swings that must be offset elsewhere through lift rotations and variations
If all your tonnage came from one evolving lift, a volume drop could lose 60% of your tonnage
Novices shouldn't use only evolving ranges because if all hit their low point at once tonnage collapses
Offset variations so they peak in volume while the heavy lift is at its lowest
Evolving ranges give mostly tiny PRs that build up over time
Don't be greedy with set evolution: a span of 3-4 sets, such as 2-5 or at most 2-6, not 1-8
A 1-15 rep range is too wide an intensity window to be useful
Strength work is the biggest plank in the water: its swings affect the whole program most
Spend more thought on evolving reps and sets for strength work than for volume work, since strength opens the session and influences the rest
